title: Step-up: the biggest lever
objectives: Show what a 10% yearly step-up does to a 15-year SIP.
Explain the order of checks: basics first, then the step-up.
body_md:
Decision point one, the step-up, is the most powerful lever a SIP investor has.

## The illustration

₹10,000 a month for 15 years, at an assumed 12% a year:

| Choice over 15 years | Invested | Value at year 15 |
|---|---|---|
| Flat ₹10,000 | ₹18.0 L | ≈ ₹50.5 L |
| ₹10,000 with a 10% yearly step-up | ≈ ₹38.1 L | ≈ ₹86.8 L |
| ₹10,000, paused for 6 months in year 5 | ₹17.4 L | ≈ ₹48.3 L |

The same start, with a step-up, ends about ₹36 lakh higher. It also invests far more, so it only works if income grows too.

## The order to do it in

Step up only after the emergency fund and loans are covered. A step-up that squeezes the budget is the first thing a client cancels in a bad month, and cancelling costs more than never having stepped up.

Module 14 covers the step-up in full: how to set the rate, the cap and the mandate, and how to keep it realistic.
example: A client earning ₹12 lakh a year, with six months of expenses saved and no personal loans, agrees to raise a ₹10,000 SIP by 10% each April, right after the increment lands.
say: A 10% step-up on the same start ends about ₹36 lakh higher in our illustration.
Let's raise it only after the emergency fund is in place.
never: Max out the step-up now and sort out the emergency fund later.

check.q: In the illustration, a 10% yearly step-up on ₹10,000 for 15 years grows to about…
check.why: About ₹86.8 L at an assumed 12%, against ₹50.5 L flat, with about ₹38.1 L invested instead of ₹18.0 L.

check.q: Which check must come before suggesting a step-up?
o: The emergency fund and any costly loans
check.why: A step-up only after the basics: six months of expenses set aside and no costly debt.

check.q: What does the illustration say a six-month pause does to a 15-year SIP?
o: It costs very little: about ₹48.3 L instead of ₹50.5 L
It has no effect at all
check.why: A short pause costs little. A yearly step-up changes the outcome far more.
